ads.headline: Lead generation interest drops; service biz ads face seasonal headwinds
actions: Shift $25/day budget toward brand awareness ads to capture off-season intent
Test seasonal service angles (e.g., 'winterize your home' for plumbers) in ad copy
Build email list now for warmer re-engagement when lead generation demand spikes
ads.source: Google Trends seasonal pattern analysis + r/FacebookAds lead gen discussions

creative.headline: Unable to provide strategy — no engagement data available this week
actions: I need actual performance data (views, likes, comments, shares, DM rates) to identify your best-performing hook
Google Trends data shows 0-100 across all metrics, and no complaint/failure data provided — this suggests either no posts this week or data collection gap
I cannot ethically recommend content angles or identify reach-killers without real engagement signals from your audience
creative.source: Incomplete data set — Google Trends only (all zeros), no Instagram Insights, no audience feedback logged

critic.headline: Most failing ads this week have no clear offer — just a service name
actions: Open your current ad — does it have a specific outcome and deadline, or just your service name?
If your CTA is 'Learn More' or 'Contact Us' — change it to 'Get a Free Quote' or similar action
Check your click-to-lead rate: if under 15%, your offer is the problem, not the audience

competitors.headline: No one is teaching service businesses HOW to respond to leads from ads
actions: Uncovered angle: competitors teach how to get leads but never what to say when the lead comes in — film 'exact script I tell my clients to use when someone fills in the form'
Pain point from this week: 'I got leads from my ads but none of them booked' — hook: 'You got leads but nobody booked. Here is exactly why and how to fix it in one message'
Top accounts posting 3-4x per week minimum with one Reel hitting 10k+ views acting as top of funnel — post volume is the differentiator right now
